Resolves #19170

Metrics and Commits can return from one native popup as one stack. Native source admission keeps the stable owner pane and accepts only a complete, same-Group center subtree. Workstation's film now moves the actual frame across measured dock targets and returns it through the existing atomic transfer and empty-window close. Cancellation settles dispatched movement before recovery; tagged recovery retires the superseded placement write.

Evidence: L3 (headed Chrome physical-window movement, live Neural Link state and continuous film rehearsal) → L3 required. No close-target residuals. Final footage, voice placement and film acceptance remain with #15252.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `DockCrossWindowParticipation.spec.mjs`: complete registered stack, stable owner and legacy singleton control; headed two-pane witness. |
| AC-2 | Same owning spec: empty, missing/root-equal center, non-edge root, mixed catalog and foreign Group refusals. Global root-transfer rejection is unchanged. |
| AC-3 | `WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL.spec.mjs`: one new Group `transferNode`, both identities, ordered projection/close phases, physical source exit. `DockPlacement.spec.mjs` covers cancelled buffered movement independently of a second window. |
| AC-4 | `GestureDriver.spec.mjs` covers pending movement, destruction, adopted outcome and successor-route isolation. The film preserves its scene ids and 93s planned budget; its continuous auto-gated rehearsal asserts multiple live previews and both returned panes. |
| AC-5 | Outside-CI headed commands below; owning unit suites execute in CI. |

The tagged-placement cancellation repair belongs in the engine Placement owner; the ticket and Contract Ledger now include it. Native preview observation reads the live DragTarget coordinator, which may differ from Participation's optional injected config.

NEO_E2E_RUN_ID=19170-b596799330 npx playwright test test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL.spec.mjs test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationFilmTourNL.spec.mjs -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --headed --workers=1 -g 'under autoGates|a popup moved|two-pane'

The first continuous rehearsal failed the new multi-preview assertion: the perimeter route reused the saved-home target. The final route crosses a measured foreign dock zone before returning home. The Placement cancellation control was red before the fix: its buffered intermediate position overwrote the recovered position.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** the perimeter leg is time-bound against a time-based commit. Each leg is `moveSteps × moveDelay` = 8 × 33 ≈ 264 ms of physical movement over `heavy-tabs`, while `DragCoordinator.nativeWindowDropDwellMs` is 1200 ms — a 4.5× margin on your machine. A host that stretches that leg past the dwell would adopt the stack into the foreign zone; the executor's `transferStarted()` guard turns that into a named failure (`native return settled before its final target`, then `finish(true)` reporting `applied: false` because the items are not in the stored home), so the failure class is a red replay, never a silent wrong commit. Watch-item for the take on the second display: if a replay ever reds there, the falsifier is the leg duration against `nativeWindowDropDwellMs`, not the admission rule.

I also actively looked for (1) a consumer that resolves `nativeEffect.transactionId` against Group history — none: `Main.mjs:1168` checks the two strings' shape, `Placement`, `DragCoordinator:1257` and `WindowPosition:256` treat the effect as a marker, so `Neo.getId('native-return')` cannot collide with a row; (2) a late input after destruction — the catch awaits `run.pending`, `endNativeGesture` + `clearNativeWindowDropCandidate` run only on the original route (`liveRoute()`), and the successor-route arm pins that a replacement route keeps its own candidate and hover; (3) a prototype-vs-own-member trap in the settle path — `waitForCrossWindowTransfer` is a prototype method, so it survives `core.Base#destroy` stripping own members, and with `settle` it borrows only the workspace's `timeout`. No concerns.
